question.problem: If $T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 9 & -8 & 10 \\ -3 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T$, then $\text{rank}(T)=$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{rank}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Im}(T))=\text{rank}(T).$ 

So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 9 & -8 & 10 \\ -3 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $3$ pivot column, we have that 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=3.
$$
